author: lrjonas
body:
O que eu fiz: Fiz um card para apresentar os audios na modal, nesses cards há a funcionalidade de adicionar audios e remover somente clicando no botão add/remove, implemntei a lógica para que o player toque somente os audios de uma playlist e na ordem em que for apresentada na view, utlizei os mesmos cards de audio na aba de playlists, implementei a lógica para que o menu suspenso de um audio publico apenas apareça a opção para remover o audio da playlist, e os audios que estiverem na playlist que forem do usuário logado, aperece somente as opções de editar e deletar, corrigi o bug da modal que não abria direto na hora que clicava na opção add to playlist.

Como testar: 

- [x] Faça o Login
- [x] Adicione alguns audios
- [x] Crie uma playlist
- [x] Faça o logout
- [x] Entre em um outra conta
- [x] Cadastre um audio como público
- [x] Faça o logaout
- [x] Entre na sua conta que foi feito a playlist
- [x] No card de playlist clique nos 3 pontos
- [x] No menu suspenso, clique em Add in this playlist
- [x] Verique se o audio criado na outra conta com o atributo público está listado 
- [x] Na modal, clique em Add para adicionar o audio a playlist
- [x] Adicione o audio que foi criado na outra conta como público
- [x] Na opção Add dos audios adicionados deverá aparecer Remove
- [x] Clique na opção Remove de algum dos audios que foram adicionados
- [x] Verifique se o audio que foi adicionado e removido dentro da modal aparece na playlist
- [x] Escolha um audio para tocar, e logo após avance alguns audios e volte alguns para verificar se está trocando para o próximo audio ou o anterior
- [x] Clique nos 3 pontos do card do audio com atributo público
- [x] Verifique se apenas a opção de remover da playlist está aparecenndo
- [x] Clique nos 3 pontos de um card que você criou na conta logada
- [x] Verifique se está aparecendo apenas as opções de editar e deletar o audio
- [x] Volte para a home
- [x] Adicione todos os audios disponíveis na playlist
- [x] Feche a modal
- [x] Clique novamente em adicionar os audios
- [x] Verifique se a mensgem que ná há audios para serem adicionados aparece na modal
- [x] Entre em uma playlist que não seja a Favorites e clique em Edit, verifique se a página para edição abre
- [x] Tente modificar e depois clique em Salvar

body: Fixes #38914. Fixes #38917. ## Proposed changes: * Add a keywords section to the UI, only visible when the beta features are enabled * Make the button on this new section trigger a new generation and execute the request including a `keywords` property on the messages array * Code refactoring to make things simpler ### Other information: - [ ] Have you written new tests for your changes, if applicable? - [ ] Have you checked the E2E test CI results, and verified that your changes do not break them? - [ ] Have you tested your changes on WordPress.com, if applicable (if so, you'll see a generated comment below with a script to run)? ## Jetpack product discussion ## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use? ## Testing instructions: * Enable beta extensions, go to the block editor and add some paragraphs about something * Open the development console on the browser and enable debug messages (`localStorage.setItem( 'debug', '*' )`) * Look for the title optimization tool on the sidebar and click on the button to trigger it * Confirm you see the "processing" state as usual * Confirm the modal will show up correctly: * the keywords section is visible at the top and looks like the proposed design * the generated suggestions are present on the body of the modal * the modal is wider than the current version (max of 700px instead of 512px) * Confirm that a new generation will start when you click the "Generate again" button * Confirm you can type something on the keywords textarea and click the "Generate again" button * On the debug messages, filter for `dops:analytics` and confirm: * the tracking messages contain two new properties: `is_retry` and `has_keywords` * the `has_keywords` field is `false` when no keywords are typed, and `true` otherwise * the `is_retry` filed is generally `false`, but will turn to `true` when you are retrying the request after an error (you can force an error by setting the browser tab as offline before clicking the "Generate again" button) * On the network activity tab of the browser, look for the requests to `jetpack-ai-query` and confirm the `keywords` property is set on the `context` object: * Confirm the new section goes away and the tool works as before, with no changes, when the beta extensions are disabled Note: the provided keywords are still being ignored by the backend, so they will not affect the results

author: andrecabalo
body:
# Projeto Onboarding

Requisitos do projeto

Tecnologias Utilizadas:

- Java 21 - Spring Boot - Spring Data JPA - Banco de dados MySQL em Docker - Docker - RESTful API

Entidades Principais:

- Item - ID (UUID) - Nome - Preço - Quantidade em estoque - Carrinho - ID (UUID) - Lista de Itens (muitos para muitos) - Data de criação - Valor total (calculado)

Regras de Negócio:

- Não pode adicionar ao carrinho itens com quantidade maior do que a disponível em estoque. - O valor total do carrinho deve ser recalculado cada vez que um item é adicionado ou removido. - Não pode haver itens duplicados no carrinho. - Deve ser possível criar, atualizar e deletar itens no estoque.

Operações da API:

- Item: - Criar item - Atualizar item - Deletar item - Listar todos os itens - Buscar item por ID - Carrinho: - Criar carrinho - Adicionar item ao carrinho - Remover item do carrinho - Listar todos os carrinhos - Buscar carrinho por ID - Passos para Implementação

Configuração do Ambiente:

- Configurar o ambiente de desenvolvimento com Java 21, Spring Boot e Docker. - Criar um contêiner Docker para o banco de dados MySQL. - Criar repositório no Github para subir o projeto.

Inicializar o Projeto Spring Boot:

- Usar o Spring Initializr para criar um novo projeto Spring Boot com dependências de Spring Web, Spring Data JPA e MySQL Driver.

Configuração do Banco de Dados:

- Configurar as propriedades do banco de dados no application.properties ou application.yml do Spring Boot. - Configurar o Docker Compose para iniciar o contêiner do MySQL Database. `docker run -d --name mysql -p 3306:3306 -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root -e MYSQL_DATABASE=cart mysql:9.0.1`

Criar Entidades e Repositórios:

- Criar classes de entidade para Item e Carrinho . - Criar interfaces de repositório para Item e Carrinho que estendem JpaRepository.

Criar Serviços:

- Implementar serviços para gerenciar a lógica de negócio de Item e Carrinho . - Garantir a validação de regras de negócio, como quantidade em estoque e cálculo de valor total. - Adicionar logs ao longo da execução para ter tracking das execuções. - Configurar o Exception Handler para capturar e expor de maneira consistente os erros.

Criar Controladores REST:

- Criar controladores REST para expor endpoints para as operações de Item e Carrinho . - Seguir as melhores práticas RESTful, como usar os verbos HTTP adequados (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) e status HTTP corretos.

Testar a API:Usar o Postman ou outra ferramenta similar para testar todos os endpoints da API.

- [ ]Escrever testes unitários para garantir que as regras de negócio estão sendo aplicadas corretamente.

body:
**Component: RecipientsDisplay** **Overview:** This pull request introduces a React component named `RecipientsDisplay` that dynamically calculates and displays the number of email recipients hidden due to overflow within a paragraph element. This component addresses scenarios where the list of recipients exceeds the available width, resulting in some recipients being truncated. **Features:** - **Dynamic Hidden Count Calculation:** - The component uses `useRef` to access the paragraph element and calculate its visible width. - It iterates over child elements (email addresses and commas) to determine if they are completely hidden from view due to overflow. - A state variable `hiddenCount` keeps track of the number of hidden recipients, updating dynamically based on the width of the container and recipient elements. - **Responsive Behavior:** - The `getIsElementVisible` function recalculates the hidden count on window resize to ensure accuracy as the viewport changes. - **Styled Components:** - Utilizes `styled-components` for styling: - The paragraph (`

`) is styled to handle text overflow with ellipsis. - A badge is conditionally rendered to display the count of hidden recipients. **Implementation Details:** 1. **Refs and State Management:** - `useRef` is used for accessing the container and paragraph elements. - `useState` manages the count of hidden recipients. 2. **Visibility Calculation Logic:** - Calculates the width of each child element. - Compares available space against specific thresholds to determine if an element is hidden. - Updates the hidden count based on these calculations. 3. **Styling:** - Styled components ensure that the paragraph handles text overflow and the badge is styled consistently. **Usage:** - Import and use `RecipientsDisplay` component to manage and display overflowed recipient counts in responsive designs. This PR enhances the user experience by providing clear feedback on hidden content and ensuring that overflow issues are handled gracefully.

author: stephprince
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/issues/1137 and fixes https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/issues/1096. 

On build, multidimensional string lists/arrays were being converted into 1-D lists/arrays:

`[['aa', 'bb'], ['cc', 'dd']] -> ["['aa', 'bb']", "['cc', 'dd']"]`.

On write, the shape of a multidimensional string dataset was being defined incorrectly and so the dataset could not be written. The data shape definition was being caught by this conditional that I believe is intended to check for structured arrays / compound data types:

https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/blob/7426275cacc769a10ffca89836765df1355ba9db/src/hdmf/backends/hdf5/h5tools.py#L1472-L1473

 I updated the conditional and `get_data_shape` is now used to set the shape of the dataset for multidimensional string lists/arrays.



## How to test the behavior?

This came up in https://github.com/NeurodataWithoutBorders/pynwb/pull/1924.

body:
- simplify and use `calendar.el` function to check if date is in the Gregorian calendar

I don't understand this part in the old function's `or`:

````
....
(when (or (string-match-p
               (rx bol (= 4 digit) "-" (= 2 digit) "-" (= 2 digit) eol)
               basename)
              ;; Wild trick: pretend to return a date even outside the dailies
              ;; dir, so that we can jump to "next" and "previous" relative to
              ;; when this file was created!
              (and (not (string-blank-p org-node-datestamp-format))
                   (string-match (org-node--make-regexp-for-time-format
                                  org-node-datestamp-format)
                                 basename)
                   (org-node--extract-ymd (match-string 0 basename)
                                          org-node-datestamp-format)))
      basename))
````

The old function just throws errors for buffers with names like `9999-01-05` or `1923-42-02` etc.

And I don't see why it does anything special outside of the dailies directory, since the rest of the old function doesn't seem to check for the directory anyway.

author: jealous
body:
Upgrade nf-float plugin to 0.4.3. This version includes a fix that sometimes the job status in MMC is not updated to Nextflow properly.

The root cause is that we depend on a full job list for individual job status update.  But sometimes the full poll doesn't take place or doesn't finish in time.

The fix is to create the status entry for each job in the plugin right after we submit a job to MMC.

Regression test has been run with nf-core/rnaseq test profile on MMC.

The change is available at:
https://github.com/MemVerge/nf-float/pull/74

author: adamdiel
body:
Hey @coldshouldermedia ! 

This PR is intended to make this repo a bit more portable between environments. I made sure to update the example `private.py` file to include all the changes below. 

The discord channels that we pass music metadata and log messages too I've made a param that you can include in our local `private.py` file. 

I also made the location of `ffmpeg` a param since on my environment its not a `.exe` 

For whatever reason on my environment, I need to define where the opus library is to get this to work. I believe I've written that addition in a way that should be of no change to your workflow. 

And finally - I flipped the switch back to false for restricting channels but in the example `private.py` file included instructions on how to overwrite that as well. This way you won't need to check in any identifying info like channel IDs anymore. 

Let me know what you think!

The `lookahead_levelset_at_xstar` in `lookahead_utils,py` has several divisions where the denominator could be 0.

Serebil's tweet on Steenee's distribution was on 15th Aug 00:41 UTC so there is possibility those on the UTC -1 to UTC -11 timezone could redeemed it on the 14th Aug 2024.

i made the necessary changes to the date and also .pkl had been replaced.

thank you for the help provided by Lusamine and Manu

Removes unused `ElementType`s in `@Target` annotations. The current approach is to only remove `ElementType`s, not add them, so we don't accidentally make a non `TYPE_USE` annotation into a `TYPE_USE` annotation, for example.

I also addressed two small bugs I encountered:
- When all the wildcard import are JDK imports, synthetic classes should be generated in the current package instead of the first wildcard import package
- Don't throw an exception when an annotation is applied on a package declaration

Instead of creating a new test case for this, I just modified one of the existing ones (`SyntheticAnnotationTargetTest`), since it's purpose already seemed to fit this PR.

Thanks!

```

Fixes ARO-9570

### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR adds a MachineConfigs for the ARO operator to lay down:

99-master-aro-etc-hosts-gateway-domains
99-worker-aro-etc-hosts-gateway-domains

During the UDR installation incident we have gone back and forth on how resolve the root issue. The root cause is that the gateway domains are not populated for OpenShift images to be pulled and installed. These domains are IPs so we can pass them into `/etc/hosts` to resolve them before other DNS resolution options are available.

author: ealsur
body:
## Scenario

Metadata read requests (not item operations) can be routed to any available regions. Metadata write requests, should always be routed to the primary / hub region.

In cases where the account is Single Write Region, this rule applies correctly.

The SDK allows users to define a list of Preferred Regions to route requests preferably. This preference applies in the following way:

* Single Write Region: Affects read operations
* Multi Write Region: Affects read and write operations

## Problem

The problem is that the above rules should apply for Item operations. Metadata operations, even on a Multi Write Region account, cannot be routed to secondary regions.

Currently when routing requests, the Global Endpoint Manager is treating all requests the same way and for Metadata write operations and Multi Write Region accounts, it will apply the user preference.

## Solution

Take into consideration the Resource Type when deciding if it's possible to route write operations to preferred regions and only do it for Item operations.

Similar code path in .NET

https://github.com/Azure/azure-cosmos-dotnet-v3/blob/2fbc27835fde0837d4b3efea0f722c5f5c64119e/Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos/src/Routing/LocationCache.cs#L530-L535

author: aarsilv
body:
_Eppo Internal_:
🎟️ **Ticket:** [FF-3037 - Optimize Java SDK getMD5Hex() to not use BigInteger](https://linear.app/eppo/issue/FF-3037/optimize-java-sdk-getmd5hex-to-not-use-biginteger)
🗨️ **Slack:** ["...they're specifically calling out the java sdk using biginteger calculations which is taking up most of the overhead..."](https://eppo-group.slack.com/archives/C04KR1GGE3C/p1723562511849529?thread_ts=1723561977.939239&cid=C04KR1GGE3C)

Profiling our Java SDK, there were a few inefficiencies in the way we computed the MD5 hash as a String, and the way we used hashing to generate an integer within a shard space:
* Hasing used `BigInteger`, which was inefficient
* Shard space generating used the string hash to then compute a number, which is an unnecessary middle step

This PR refactors `getMD5hash()` to not use `BigInteger`, and `getShard()` to not use `getMD5Hash()`.

It puts in place a test that generates 10,000 assignments and asserts that it computes quickly. Using that test, it seems these optimizations generate about a 6x speed up.

author: chris1984
body:
#### What are the changes introduced in this pull request?
* Changed the int4 column on `convert2rhel_through_foreman` from `init4` to `boolean`
* Return out of the fact parser method for hosts that are not registered such as foreman/satellite instance, so we don't error when those systems upload facts
* Got rid of `build_subscription_facet` because the hosts that come from convert2rhel already are registered and have a subscription facet, so no need to build one which also breaks hosts that are not registered through subscription-manager
* If for some reason we hit an edge case where we don't get the convert2rhel fact the first time during registration , we will get it when the client checks in again ~ 4 hours. Talking with Shim and Jeremy this seems like a fine approach since the systems `rhsmcertd` will send us the filtered fact again, which is more than enough time before `rh_cloud` would send off it's report to `console.redhat.com`

https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/converting-centos-rhel-convert2rhel-and-satellite

#### What are the testing steps for this pull request?
* Apply PR
* Run DB Migration
* Try the following curl command on your devel box and make sure it uploads facts and does not return `"error": {"message":"Content host must be unregistered before performing this action."}`

```

author: nateprewitt
body: This PR fixes missing brackets from the `Host` header when supplying a hostname that matches an IP-literal as defined in [RFC 3986 3.2.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.2.2). This will resolve issues between how we're signing requests and how they're being interpreted by AWS services which is currently leading to signature mismatches.
